approach: Learned GAN fingerprints for detection and closed-set source attribution
model: Deep CNN attribution classifier (fingerprint = final 1x1x512 feature/weight tensors); AutoEncoder visualisation variant
dataset: CelebA and LSUN bedroom (20,000 reals each; 100K train / 10K test per source)
generators: ProGAN, SNGAN, CramerGAN, MMDGAN (all 128x128x3)
result: 99.43% (CelebA) / 98.58% (LSUN) on 5-class {real + 4 GANs} attribution, vs PRNU baseline 86.61 / 67.84
limitation: Needs source-labelled samples from every candidate GAN; evaluated only at 128x128

approach: PRNU-style handcrafted fingerprint: averaged denoising residuals, correlation-based source identification
model: Denoising-filter residual averaging (no learned classifier)
dataset: 1,000 RGB 256x256 images per source; RAISE camera images; CycleGAN / ProGAN / StarGAN category sets
generators: CycleGAN (9 configs), ProGAN (6 configs), StarGAN (5 configs)
result: Source-attribution accuracy 90.3% uncompressed, 90.1% after JPEG QF=95
crossgen: No — source ID among known GANs
limitation: Weaker on StarGAN male/smiling networks and on real cameras (low-energy PRNU patterns)

approach: Spectrum classifier aimed at GAN upsampling artefacts; an AutoGAN simulator creates them, so no real fakes are needed
model: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-34 on the log frequency spectrum, phase dropped
dataset: 14-category CycleGAN image sets; AutoGAN trained on 4,000 MSCOCO images
generators: CycleGAN mainly; StarGAN, GauGAN tested too
result: AutoGAN-trained spectrum classifier, never shown a real fake: 97.2% mean leave-one-out accuracy
crossgen: Yes – simulated artefacts expose unseen GANs
limitation: Every classifier fails on GauGAN, which upsamples differently; hurt by upsampler mismatch

approach: Pixel-domain co-occurrence matrices fed to a deep CNN
model: Deep CNN on 3-channel co-occurrence matrices
dataset: Two GAN datasets, 56,000+ images (unpaired translation; facial attributes)
generators: CycleGAN, StarGAN
result: >99% classification accuracy on both datasets
crossgen: Yes — trained one GAN, tested the other
limitation: Only two GAN families evaluated; no explicit limitation stated in abstract

approach: Frequency-domain forensics: azimuthally averaged 1D power spectrum + classical classifier
model: SVM (RBF), logistic regression, K-means (unsupervised)
dataset: Faces-HQ (40K, self-assembled), CelebA, FaceForensics++
generators: Self-trained DCGAN; fakes from thispersondoesnotexist.com; FF++ manipulations
result: 100% accuracy on Faces-HQ with as few as 20 labelled samples; 91% accuracy on FF++ videos
limitation: Low-resolution content harder to identify since the available frequency spectrum is much smaller

approach: Two-class real-vs-fake CNN; Blur+JPEG augmentation and careful pre- and post-processing
model: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50
dataset: ForenSynths: 720K ProGAN training images, LSUN reals, 11-generator test sets
generators: Train: ProGAN; 11 test sets: ProGAN, StyleGAN, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, DeepFakes, CRN, IMLE, SAN, SITD; StyleGAN2 tested separately
result: Averaged across 11 test sets (ProGAN and 10 unseen generators): mAP 90.1 without augmentation, 90.8 with Blur+JPEG(0.5)
crossgen: Yes – trained on ProGAN; 10 of the 11 test generators unseen
limitation: Chance-level on traditional (Photoshop-style) edits; the authors hedge with "for now"

approach: Patch-based classification with limited receptive fields; heatmaps of which patches are detectable
model: Truncated Xception and ResNet patch classifiers (Xception blocks best)
dataset: CelebA-HQ (24,183 train), FFHQ (60,000 train), FaceForensics++
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, Glow, GMM face generator; FF++ manipulations
result: AP 99.99 training on ProGAN and testing on StyleGAN; AP ~100 across unseen resolutions
limitation: "No method is completely bulletproof" — better generators, out-of-distribution images or adversarial attacks can defeat it

approach: DCT frequency-domain analysis of grid-like upsampling artefacts with simple classifiers
model: Ridge regression and a shallow 4-conv-layer CNN (~170K params) on DCT spectra
dataset: FFHQ, CelebA, LSUN bedrooms
generators: StyleGAN, BigGAN, ProGAN, SN-DCGAN, CramerGAN, MMDGAN
result: Ridge-Regression-DCT 100.00% real-vs-fake on FFHQ (vs 75.78% on pixels); CNN-DCT source ID 99.64% LSUN / 99.07% CelebA
limitation: Classifier can still be evaded by specifically crafted adversarial perturbations

approach: Azimuthal integration of the DFT power spectrum into a 1D feature + classical classifiers; proposes spectral regularisation
model: SVM, logistic regression, K-means (unsupervised) on the spectral feature
dataset: Faces-HQ (40K, self-built), CelebA (202,599), FaceForensics++
generators: DCGAN, DRAGAN, LSGAN, WGAN-GP (CelebA); FaceForensics++ deepfakes
result: 100% on Faces-HQ (SVM, 1000 samples) and 100% on CelebA (2000 samples); 85% on FF++ single frames
limitation: Detection assumes up-convolution generators; other generation techniques may not show these signatures

approach: Global texture (Gram) statistics for fake face detection
model: Gram-Net (CNN leveraging global texture representations)
dataset: CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, CelebA (real); GAN face sets; ImageNet / BigGAN (natural)
generators: StyleGAN, PGGAN, DCGAN, DRAGAN, StarGAN, BigGAN
result: ~77.7% accuracy cross-GAN (train StyleGAN, test DCGAN / DRAGAN / StarGAN); >98% in-domain
limitation: Analysis covers only texture contrast; real/fake differences go beyond it

approach: High-frequency Fourier spectral-decay analysis (fitted decay parameters)
model: KNN (k=5) on the fitted decay parameters
dataset: FFHQ + Cat Head Detection dataset (~5,000 images, 10/90 train/test)
generators: StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, PGGAN, VQ-VAE2, ALAE
result: 99.2% accuracy on uncompressed 1024x1024 images, mixed-generator training
crossgen: No — five generators, none held out
limitation: At 85% JPEG compression generated spectra become essentially indistinguishable from real; 88.8% at 256x256

approach: Critical benchmark of state-of-the-art GAN-image detectors under compression, resizing and unseen generators
model: Seven detectors: Xception, SRNet, Spec, M-Gb, Co-Net, Wang2020 ResNet50, PatchForensics + proposed no-down variant
dataset: 362K LSUN reals + 362K ProGAN fakes (train); test reals from ImageNet, COCO, RAISE (~39K synthetic test)
generators: ProGAN (train); tested StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, RelGAN, GauGAN
result: AUC above 0.9 for several methods on uncompressed unseen GANs; severe drops after compression/resizing; best no-down variant above 90% accuracy
limitation: Authors state "we are still very far from having reliable tools for GAN image detection"; robustness experiments preliminary

approach: Contrastive learning with limited sub-sampling architecture
model: ResNet50 (ImageNet-pretrained, no first-layer subsampling) + 2 projection layers
dataset: LSUN (362K real) + 362K ProGAN images (train); ImageNet, COCO, RAISE (test)
generators: ProGAN (train); StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, RelGAN, GauGAN (unseen test)
result: 95.6% accuracy / 0.997 AUC averaged over unseen GAN architectures
limitation: Robustness to adversarial attacks left to future work

approach: Counter-study of high-frequency spectral-decay features, showing the artefact is removable via upsampling choice
model: KNN (k=5) on 3 spectral features (also SVM, MLP); GANs retrained with modified last-layer upsampling
dataset: CelebA (128), LSUN Bedrooms (128), CelebA-HQ (512)
generators: DCGAN, LSGAN, WGAN-GP, StarGAN (+CRN, IMLE supplementary)
result: Detection rate collapses to 0–0.3% with bilinear upsampling vs 84.8–99.8% baseline
limitation: Its own finding: high-frequency spectral decay is not intrinsic to CNN-generated images, so detectors built on it are unreliable

approach: Frequency-level perturbation maps (FrePGAN) to suppress frequency artefacts
model: Perturbation generator + ResNet-50 deepfake classifier
dataset: ProGAN-generated train set; test images from FFHQ, LSUN, ImageNet, CelebA, COCO, Deepfake sets
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN
result: 79.4% average accuracy / 87.2% average precision cross-model (4-class training)
crossgen: Yes — known and unseen GAN models
limitation: Tradeoff: frequency artefacts aid known-GAN detection but reduce cross-GAN generalisation

approach: Ensemble of orthogonally trained CNNs favouring real-image scores
model: Ensemble of five EfficientNet-B4 CNNs
dataset: FFHQ, Metfaces, AFHQ2 (~116K real) + ~200K synthetic (train); StyleGAN3 test pairs
generators: StyleGAN2, StarGAN-v2, Taming Transformers, FaceVid2Vid, score-based models; StyleGAN3 (unseen)
result: 0.9995 AUC on the global test set including unseen StyleGAN3
limitation: Orthogonality among the CNNs is only empirically verified; no theoretical grounding

approach: Fusion of global spatial and local patch features via attention
model: Two-branch ResNet-50 (ImageNet-pretrained) + patch selection module + multi-head attention
dataset: Self-built diverse test set: 128,424 images from 19 generation models
generators: 19 models incl. ProGAN, StyleGAN/2/3, BigGAN, WGAN, VAEGAN, GauGAN, StarGAN, CycleGAN, Pix2Pix, FF++, Celeb-DF
result: 91.73% mean AP on unseen models (96.91% global AP mixed)
limitation: Resizing high-resolution images makes artefacts harder to detect

approach: Bilateral high-pass filters (frequency-level + pixel-level) amplifying frequency artefacts
model: ResNet-50 classifier with a BiHPF front-end
dataset: LSUN, FFHQ (real); ProGAN images for training
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN
result: 84.2% mean accuracy / 81.8% mean AP on unseen GAN models (4-class ProGAN training)
limitation: No limitations stated; evaluation covers GAN generators only

approach: ViT compared with a CNN classifier across forgery types
model: EfficientNetV2-M vs ViT-Base
dataset: ForgeryNet: 15 manipulation methods
generators: GAN, reenactment and swap methods, e.g. ATVG-net, Deepfakes, FaceShifter, FS-GAN, StyleGAN2, Talking Head Video
result: Trained on three face-transfer methods: EfficientNetV2-M 81.1% on one but 47.0% and 57.0% on the other two; ViT-Base ~62.0% on all three
crossgen: Yes – subset training, testing on 15 methods
limitation: Accuracy on new, unseen methods stays fairly low

approach: Learning on Gradients (LGrad): gradients from a pretrained CNN as a generalised artefact representation
model: Pretrained-CNN transformation model converting images to gradients + classifier
dataset: ForenSynths / CNNDetection training set: 20 ProGAN categories, 18,000 fake + 18,000 real each; 1-, 2- and 4-class settings
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, Deepfake (8 test models)
result: 86.3% mean ACC / 92.7% mean AP over the 8 test models (1-class setting); +11.4% ACC and +13.4% AP over FrePGAN
limitation: Turns a data-dependent problem into a transformation-model-dependent one (authors' own framing)

approach: Analyses forensic traces (spectral fingerprints) of diffusion models and evaluates existing detectors
model: Spec, PatchForensics, Wang2020 (augmentation-trained ResNet-50), Grag2021 (first-layer downsampling removed)
dataset: Real: COCO, ImageNet, UCID; fakes from COCO prompts
generators: ADM, DALL-E 2, GLIDE, Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion; references: BigGAN, EG3D, ProGAN, StyleGAN2/3
result: Averaged over 12 test generators (the training GAN and 5 diffusion models included): AUC ~75–93% and accuracy ~52–76% uncompressed; accuracy ~50–61% after resizing and compression
crossgen: Yes – GAN-trained detectors run on diffusion images
limitation: Generalisation is still the chief obstacle; GAN-trained detectors do badly on diffusion images, more so once compressed or resized

approach: Diffusion reconstruction error (DIRE): residual between an image and its DDIM reconstruction
model: ResNet-50 classifier on DIRE maps; ADM (LSUN-Bedroom) reconstructor, DDIM 20 steps
dataset: DiffusionForensics benchmark (LSUN-Bedroom, ImageNet sources)
generators: 8 diffusion models: ADM, DDPM, iDDPM, PNDM, LDM, SD-v1, SD-v2, VQ-Diffusion
result: 99.9% average accuracy / 100 AP across 8 diffusion models including unseen ones (ADM-trained)
crossgen: Yes — generalises to unseen diffusion models
limitation: No limitations stated; scope limited to diffusion-generated images

approach: Text-to-image fake detection and attribution via image-only and hybrid (image+prompt) classifiers
model: ResNet18 (image-only); CLIP image + text encoders with a 2-layer MLP (hybrid)
dataset: MSCOCO, Flickr30k (real) + fakes from four text-to-image models
generators: Stable Diffusion, Latent Diffusion, GLIDE, DALL-E 2
result: Hybrid detector trained on SD: accuracy 0.932 / 0.899 / 0.885 on Latent Diffusion / GLIDE / DALL-E 2 (MSCOCO)
crossgen: Yes — SD-trained, three unseen T2I models
limitation: Image-only detection "far from the design goal" on other models such as GLIDE and DALL-E 2

approach: Stepwise error between the deterministic reverse and denoising diffusion steps (SeDID)
model: SeDID_Stat (statistical) and SeDID_NNs (neural network) variants
dataset: CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, CelebA (all 32x32)
generators: DDPM only
result: SeDID_NNs: average AUC 0.9634 / ACC 0.9399 across the three datasets
crossgen: No — DDPM only, no other families
limitation: Dataset-dependent optimal timestep selection; unusual trends on CelebA need further investigation

approach: Analysis-only forensic study of spectral/frequency artefacts in synthetic images; no detector proposed
model: None; power-spectrum, autocorrelation and radial/angular spectral analyses
dataset: Real: ImageNet, FFHQ, LAION; fakes from 15 models
generators: GANs: BigGAN, StyleGAN2/3, StyleGAN-T, GALIP; VQ models; DMs: Score-SDE, ADM, GLIDE, DALL-E 2, eDiff-I; latent DMs: LDM, SD, DiT
result: None; artefacts characterised through spectral analyses, no detection metrics
limitation: Post-processing, the authors note, "may significantly modify and hide" these artefacts

approach: Real-vs-fake classification without training the backbone: nearest-neighbour or linear probing in a frozen vision-language feature space
model: CLIP ViT-L/14 visual encoder (last-layer features) + NN or linear probe
dataset: ProGAN real/fake training set (720k images); ForenSynths + diffusion / autoregressive test sets
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, CRN, IMLE, SAN, SITD, DeepFakes, Guided, LDM, Glide, DALL-E
result: +15.07 mAP / +25.90% accuracy over the previous state of the art on unseen diffusion and autoregressive models
limitation: Why the frozen CLIP feature space separates real from fake "remains an open question"

approach: Million-scale benchmark defining cross-generator and degraded-image evaluation tasks
model: ResNet-50, DeiT-S, Swin-T, CNNSpot, Spec, F3Net, GramNet
dataset: GenImage: >1M fake pairs + 1,331,167 ImageNet reals
generators: Midjourney, SD v1.4, SD v1.5, ADM, GLIDE, Wukong, VQDM, BigGAN
result: ResNet-50 accuracy 99.9% same-generator (SD v1.4) but 54.9% tested on Midjourney
crossgen: Yes — defines a cross-generator classification task
limitation: Detectors degrade sharply cross-generator and on low-resolution, JPEG-compressed and blurred images

approach: Large-scale dataset + multi-class classification with filter stride reduction
model: ConvNeXt-Large (modified stem)
dataset: ArtiFact: 2,496,738 images (964,989 real / 1,531,749 fake)
generators: 25 methods: 13 GANs, 7 diffusion, 5 miscellaneous
result: Accuracy 96.04% / 83.00% / 90.60% on IEEE VIP Cup 2022 Tests 1–3
crossgen: Yes — unseen generators in challenge tests
limitation: State-of-the-art detectors still struggle on generators unseen during training

approach: Interpretable prototype-based detection via ViT features + SVM support vectors
model: Fine-tuned ViT + SVM (repo also uses xDNN, KNN, Naive Bayes)
dataset: Custom datasets built from ImageNet, FFHQ, Oxford-IIIT Pet
generators: Diffusion models (Stable Diffusion; various diffusion generative techniques)
result: Within-dataset best 99.5% (Oxford-IIIT Pet), 96.7% (image-to-image ImageNet), 99.7% (class-conditional ImageNet), 99.4% (FFHQ) with fine-tuned ViT + MLP head; SVM on fine-tuned features 93.0–97.2%; cross-dataset 81.3% and 84.0%
crossgen: No — cross-dataset only, no unseen-generator test
limitation: Lack of open datasets; evaluated only on self-created custom datasets

approach: Neighbouring Pixel Relationships (NPR) capturing up-sampling artefacts
model: Lightweight CNN (conv layers + ResNet blocks, 1.44M params) on NPR
dataset: ForenSynths ProGAN 4-class train (car, cat, chair, horse; 18K fake + 18K real per class)
generators: 28 generative models: 16 GANs, 1 deepfake method, 11 diffusion models
result: 92.2% mean accuracy across 28 generators (+11.6% over the prior state of the art)
crossgen: Yes — 28 unseen GAN and diffusion models
limitation: No explicit limitation stated; trained solely on ProGAN 4-class data

approach: Frequency-space learning: high-frequency image/feature representations + convolution in the FFT domain
model: FreqNet — lightweight CNN with residual blocks, no pretraining, 1.9M parameters
dataset: ForenSynths (ProGAN training, 1/2/4-class) + GAN self-synthesis test sets
generators: 17 GANs incl. ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, AttGAN, plus a Deepfake set
result: 92.8% mean accuracy over 17 GAN test sets, +9.8% over Ojha (83.0%)
limitation: No limitations stated in the conclusion; evaluation restricted to GAN sources

approach: Benchmark of GAN detectors on diffusion images + frequency-domain artefact analysis + retraining
model: Wang2020 (ResNet-50), Gragnaniello2021, Mandelli2022 (EfficientNet-B4 ensemble)
dataset: LSUN Bedroom 256 (primary); LSUN Cat/Horse, ImageNet, FFHQ extensions
generators: 5 GANs (ProGAN, StyleGAN, ProjectedGAN, Diff-StyleGAN2, Diff-ProjectedGAN) + 5 DMs (DDPM, IDDPM, ADM, PNDM, LDM)
result: GAN detectors drop on average 15.2% AUROC on DM images; a DM-trained detector reaches 94.26% average Pd@1%FAR on GANs, a GAN-trained one only 26.34% on DMs
limitation: DMs leave fewer detectable artefacts, and perturbations degrade DM detectability more strongly

approach: Training-free detection via autoencoder reconstruction error of latent diffusion models
model: Pretrained LDM autoencoders + reconstruction distance (LPIPS); no trained classifier
dataset: Real images from LAION-5B + prompt-matched generated counterparts (Midjourney set from Discord)
generators: Stable Diffusion 1.1/1.5/2.1, Kandinsky 2.1, Midjourney 4/5/5.1
result: Mean AP 0.992 across state-of-the-art LDMs including SD, Kandinsky and Midjourney
crossgen: Yes — multiple LDMs incl. proprietary Midjourney
limitation: Best results require access to the generating LDM's autoencoder; method scoped to latent diffusion

approach: Latent reconstruction error (LaRE) feature for diffusion-image detection
model: LaRE feature + Error-Guided feature REfinement module (EGRE, spatial + channel align-then-refine)
dataset: GenImage benchmark
generators: 8 image generators (GenImage subsets)
result: Surpasses the state of the art by up to 11.9% / 12.1% average ACC / AP across 8 generators on GenImage
limitation: Residual real/fake feature overlap on unseen generators (Midjourney, ADM, BigGAN); LaRE alone insufficient as sole input

approach: Exposing and removing JPEG-compression and image-size biases in detection datasets
model: ResNet50 and Swin-T detectors
dataset: GenImage
generators: Midjourney, SD v1.4, SD v1.5, Wukong, VQDM, ADM, GLIDE, BigGAN
result: Bias-corrected training raises cross-generator accuracy by >11 pp on GenImage: ResNet50 71.68% -> 82.74%, Swin-T 74.09% -> 85.83%
limitation: Even with constraints, "datasets may contain other undesirable biases" (style differences, generator fingerprints)

approach: Contrastive training on diffusion-reconstructed hard samples (DRCT framework)
model: ConvNeXt-B and CLIP-ViT-L/14 (UnivFD) backbones
dataset: DRCT-2M (proposed, million-scale), GenImage; real images from MSCOCO
generators: 16 types of diffusion models (incl. SD v1.4 / v2)
result: Over 10% accuracy improvement in cross-set tests (trained on SD v1.4, tested on GenImage subsets)
crossgen: Yes — unseen diffusion models, cross-set tests
limitation: Improvement on non-diffusion (GAN) images is less marked; covers only globally generated images, not local regions

approach: Detection via Stable Diffusion inversion features
model: ResNet50 trained from scratch on the concatenated image + decoded noise map + reconstruction
dataset: Real: LAION, WebLI, reverse-image-search sets; new SynRIS benchmark (15 eval sets)
generators: Trained on SD; evaluated on 15+ models incl. DALL-E 2/3, Midjourney, Imagen, Kandinsky 2/3, PixArt-alpha, SDXL, Playground 2.5, Stable Cascade
result: Average AUC-ROC 0.759 across the tested generators under the RIS protocol (trained on SD+LAION)
crossgen: Yes — SD-trained, unseen T2I models tested
limitation: May not transfer to non-diffusion text-to-image models (GANs, transformers); the inversion pipeline needs significantly more compute

approach: Zero-shot entropy-based forensics: coding cost under a model of real images, trained on real images only
model: Lossless multi-resolution neural image encoder (ZED)
dataset: Open Images (~338k real images) for encoder training; 19-generator synthetic test set
generators: 19 generators incl. GauGAN, BigGAN, StyleGAN2, GigaGAN, ADM, GLIDE, SD/SDXL, DiT, DALL-E 1/2/3, Midjourney v5, Firefly
result: ~90.0% average AUC across 19 generators; >3% average accuracy gain over the state of the art
limitation: Unreliable on heavily compressed or resized images; detects fully generated images only, not local manipulations

approach: Few-shot CLIP-feature forensics: linear SVM on frozen CLIP features from a handful of reference images
model: CLIP ViT-L/14 (next-to-last-layer features) + linear SVM
dataset: Few paired real/fake reference images (10 to 10k) from a single generator; 18-generator test suite
generators: 18 generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN2/3/T, GigaGAN, Score-SDE, ADM, GLIDE, eDiff-I, LDM, SD variants, DiT, DeepFloyd-IF, DALL-E 2/3, Midjourney v5, Firefly
result: ~90.0% average AUC across 18 generators; +6% AUC out of distribution and +13% on impaired data vs the state of the art
limitation: Interpretability lacking: which forensic features CLIP exploits is not yet understood

approach: Synthetic-image detection from intermediate CLIP encoder-block representations with learnable importance weighting
model: RINE: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 intermediate blocks + a lightweight trainable projection/weighting network
dataset: ProGAN training data (1/2/4-class settings); 20 test datasets
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN/2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, DeepFake, SITD, SAN, CRN, IMLE, Guided, LDM (3), Glide (3), DALL-E
result: 91.5% average accuracy and 98.8 AP (4-class training) across 20 test sets; +10.6% ACC over the state of the art
limitation: Combined perturbations (blur + crop + compression + noise) considerably reduce performance

approach: Forgery-aware adaptive transfer of CLIP: an adapter over image and frequency domains with language-guided alignment
model: FatFormer (CLIP-ViT + forgery-aware adapter + text-prompt alignment)
dataset: ProGAN 4-class training set; unseen GAN and diffusion test sets
generators: GANs and diffusion models (unseen at test time)
result: 98% accuracy on unseen GANs, 95% on unseen diffusion models
crossgen: Yes — unseen GANs and diffusion models
limitation: Trained on ProGAN data only; authors state room to improve on diffusion models such as Guided, and that GAN vs diffusion artefact relationships remain unresolved

approach: Adapting a vision-language model (CLIP) via prompt tuning for universal detection
model: CLIP ViT (prompt tuning; compared with linear probe, fine-tuning, adapter)
dataset: ProGAN 200k train; 21 test datasets
generators: GANs, diffusion models, commercial tools
result: 98.06% mAP / 89.45% average accuracy across 18 unseen generators (prompt tuning)
limitation: Performance drops on commercial-tool images under JPEG compression

approach: CNN binary real-vs-fake classification with Grad-CAM explainability
model: Custom CNN (best of 36 topologies: 2 conv layers x32 filters + dense 64)
dataset: CIFAKE: 120,000 images (60k CIFAR-10 real + 60k synthetic)
generators: Stable Diffusion v1.4 (latent diffusion)
result: 92.98% accuracy on the CIFAKE test set
limitation: Single generator at 32px resolution; classification driven by background imperfections

approach: Quantitative framework for scoring how XAI methods explain a deepfake detector
model: Grad-CAM++, RISE, SHAP, LIME, SOBOL benchmarked on an EfficientNetV2 detector
dataset: FaceForensics++
generators: Four face manipulation methods: DeepFakes, FaceSwap, Face2Face, NeuralTextures
result: LIME best: detector accuracy left at 0.579 on NeuralTextures after altering its top segment, 0.245 on DeepFakes after its top three
limitation: Explanation methods still struggle most with Face2Face and FaceSwap fakes

approach: Supervised detector trained on a massively diverse multi-generator dataset
model: ViT-S (CLIP-pretrained) classifier; ConvNeXt-S also tested
dataset: Community Forensics (2.7M images, 4,803 generators); evaluated on Wang, Ojha, Synthbuster, GenImage + own 21-model eval set
generators: 4,803 generators: latent and pixel diffusion, GANs, commercial models
result: 0.987 mAP and 89.2% accuracy on the out-of-distribution eval set (21 unseen models)
limitation: Dataset skewed toward diffusion models; error rates still too high for critical applications

approach: Hybrid low-level (frequency/noise) and high-level (semantic) mixture-of-experts detection; proposes the in-the-wild Chameleon benchmark
model: AIDE: DCT scoring module + SRM noise filters + OpenCLIP semantic encoder
dataset: AIGCDetectBenchmark, GenImage, Chameleon (proposed)
generators: ProGAN, StyleGAN/2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, ADM, Glide, SD v1.4/1.5, VQDM, Wukong, Midjourney, DALLE-2/3
result: 92.77% mean accuracy on AIGCDetectBenchmark, 86.88% on GenImage; drops to 65.77% on Chameleon
limitation: All tested detectors near-fail on realistic Chameleon images; the problem is "far from being solved"

approach: Category-common prompt injected into the CLIP text encoder to embed detection semantics into image features
model: C2P-CLIP (CLIP ViT-L/14 with a category common prompt)
dataset: UniversalFakeDetect (ProGAN train, 19 test subsets) and GenImage (SD v1.4 train)
generators: 20 generation models (UniversalFakeDetect subsets + GenImage diffusion models)
result: 93.79% accuracy / 98.66% mAP on the 19 UniversalFakeDetect test subsets; 95.8% accuracy on GenImage
limitation: Word-frequency prompt analysis lacks full-caption analysis, giving incomplete information

approach: Effort: SVD splits frozen foundation-model features into orthogonal subspaces
model: CLIP ViT-L/14 (ablations: BEiT-v2, SigLIP)
dataset: Training: ProGAN; testing: 19 UniversalFakeDetect subsets, plus FF++ (deepfakes)
generators: ProGAN, CycleGAN, BigGAN, StyleGAN, GauGAN, StarGAN, Guided/Latent Diffusion, GLIDE, DALL-E
result: mAP 99.41%, mAcc 95.19% over 19 test subsets, unseen generators among them
crossgen: Yes – unseen generators among the 19 test subsets
limitation: Authors raise only misuse risk and discuss no technical limitations
